subject: MATH
title: Mathematics 8
description: Grade 8 mathematics following the California Common Core sequence used by Illustrative Mathematics Grade 8. Students study rigid transformations, similarity and slope, linear relationships and equations, systems of equations, functions, volume, bivariate data, exponents and scientific notation, and the Pythagorean theorem with irrational numbers. Every week mixes concept-building tasks, practice, a hands-on or graphing activity, and a Friday check.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics; 2023 CA Mathematics Framework

standards.8.NS.A.1: Know that numbers that are not rational are irrational; every number has a decimal expansion; convert repeating decimals to fractions.
standards.8.NS.A.2: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare them, locate them on a number line, and estimate expressions.
standards.8.EE.A.1: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
standards.8.EE.A.2: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to x^2 = p and x^3 = p; know small perfect squares and cubes; know sqrt 2 is irrational.
standards.8.EE.A.3: Use numbers expressed as a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities and compare them.
standards.8.EE.A.4: Perform operations with numbers in scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size; interpret technology output.
standards.8.EE.B.5: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope; compare proportional relationships represented in different ways.
standards.8.EE.B.6: Use similar triangles to explain why slope is the same between any two points on a line; derive y = mx and y = mx + b.
standards.8.EE.C.7a: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions.
standards.8.EE.C.7b: Solve linear equations with rational coefficients, including equations needing the distributive property and collecting like terms.
standards.8.EE.C.8a: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations correspond to points of intersection of their graphs.
standards.8.EE.C.8b: Solve systems of two linear equations algebraically and estimate solutions by graphing; solve simple cases by inspection.
standards.8.EE.C.8c: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.
standards.8.F.A.1: Understand that a function assigns to each input exactly one output; the graph is the set of ordered pairs.
standards.8.F.A.2: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically, verbally).
standards.8.F.A.3: Interpret y = mx + b as defining a linear function whose graph is a straight line; give examples of nonlinear functions.
standards.8.F.B.4: Construct a function to model a linear relationship; determine and interpret rate of change and initial value.
standards.8.F.B.5: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph; sketch graphs from verbal descriptions.
standards.8.G.A.1: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations (lines to lines, angles and lengths preserved, parallel lines preserved).
standards.8.G.A.2: Understand that two figures are congruent if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of rigid motions; describe the sequence.
standards.8.G.A.3: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.
standards.8.G.A.4: Understand that two figures are similar if one can be obtained from the other by rigid motions and dilations; describe the sequence.
standards.8.G.A.5: Use informal arguments about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal, and the AA criterion for similarity.
standards.8.G.B.6: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean theorem and its converse.
standards.8.G.B.7: Apply the Pythagorean theorem to find unknown side lengths in right triangles in two and three dimensions.
standards.8.G.B.8: Apply the Pythagorean theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.
standards.8.G.C.9: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve problems.
standards.8.SP.A.1: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate data; describe clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear and nonlinear association.
standards.8.SP.A.2: Know that straight lines model linear association; informally fit a line and judge closeness of fit.
standards.8.SP.A.3: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems, interpreting slope and intercept.
standards.8.SP.A.4: Understand patterns of association in categorical data using two-way tables and relative frequencies.

units.title: Rigid Transformations and Congruence
units.big_idea: Translations, rotations, and reflections move figures without changing size or shape, so congruent figures are linked by rigid motions.

units.title: Dilations, Similarity, and Slope
units.big_idea: Dilations scale figures; similar triangles explain why a line has a constant slope.

units.title: Linear Relationships
units.big_idea: A linear relationship has a constant rate of change (slope) and an initial value, and can be shown in tables, graphs, equations and words.

units.title: Linear Equations and Linear Systems
units.big_idea: Equations are solved by keeping them balanced; the solution to a system is the point that makes both equations true.

units.title: Functions and Volume
units.big_idea: A function gives exactly one output per input; volume formulas for cylinders, cones and spheres are functions of their dimensions.

units.title: Associations in Data
units.big_idea: Scatter plots and two-way tables reveal patterns of association that can be modeled and interpreted.

units.title: Exponents and Scientific Notation
units.big_idea: Exponent rules follow from repeated multiplication and let us write and compute with very large and very small numbers.

units.title: Pythagorean Theorem and Irrational Numbers
units.big_idea: In a right triangle a^2 + b^2 = c^2, and many side lengths are irrational numbers we can locate and approximate.

units.title: Putting It All Together
units.big_idea: Grade 8 tools (linear models, systems, volume, data) combine to solve open-ended real-world problems.

objectives: Describe translations, rotations and reflections in precise language
Perform rigid motions on a grid and with tracing paper

days.title: Diagnostic & moves warm-up
days.work: Take a 15-problem Grade 7 readiness check (proportions, integers, expressions); then use tracing paper to slide, turn and flip a paper cutout and describe each move in words.

days.title: Translations
days.work: Translate triangles on a grid using directed line segments; draw 4 images and label corresponding points A to A'.

days.title: Rotations
days.work: Rotate figures 90, 180 and 270 degrees clockwise and counterclockwise about a given center using tracing paper; record the center and angle for each.

days.title: Reflections
days.work: Reflect figures across horizontal, vertical and diagonal lines; complete IM Lesson 'Grid Moves' style practice of 8 problems mixing all three moves.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: identify and perform 6 single transformations and write a precise description of each; correct errors in a math notebook.

weeks.assessment: Friday quiz on performing and describing single rigid motions (80% target).

weeks.topic: Properties of rigid motions and coordinates
objectives: Verify that rigid motions preserve lengths and angle measures
Use coordinates to describe the effect of translations, rotations and reflections

days.title: Rigid motions preserve measures
days.work: Measure side lengths and angles of a polygon and its image after three different moves; write a conclusion about what stays the same.

days.title: Parallel lines stay parallel
days.work: Rotate a pair of parallel lines 180 degrees about a point using GeoGebra and explain why the images are parallel to the originals.

days.title: Coordinate translations
days.work: Translate figures on the coordinate plane and write the rule (x, y) -> (x + a, y + b) for 6 examples.

days.title: Coordinate reflections & rotations
days.work: Discover the rules for reflecting over the x- and y-axes and rotating 90 and 180 degrees about the origin by plotting and comparing coordinates.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 10-problem coordinate-transformation worksheet, then write rules from before-and-after coordinate lists.

weeks.assessment: Exit ticket: write the coordinate rule for 4 transformations and justify which properties are preserved.

weeks.topic: Congruence through sequences of rigid motions
objectives: Define congruence using rigid motions
Describe a sequence of moves that maps one figure onto a congruent figure

days.title: What is congruence?
days.work: Sort 8 pairs of figures into congruent / not congruent and justify each answer with a rigid-motion argument rather than 'looks the same'.

days.title: Sequences of moves
days.work: Find a sequence of two or three transformations mapping figure A to figure B for 6 grid problems; compare two different valid sequences.

days.title: Congruent polygons
days.work: Cut out cardstock quadrilaterals and test congruence by moving one onto the other; write the sequence used.

days.title: Points, segments and circles
days.work: Show that two segments of the same length and two circles of the same radius are congruent by describing the moves.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: describe sequences of moves for 4 pairs and explain why one pair cannot be congruent.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on congruence sequences with written justifications.

weeks.topic: Angles: parallel lines, transversals and triangles
objectives: Identify alternate interior, corresponding and vertical angles
Explain why triangle angles sum to 180 degrees

days.title: Vertical & supplementary angles
days.work: Use a 180-degree rotation to explain why vertical angles are equal; solve 8 missing-angle problems.

days.title: Parallel lines and transversals
days.work: Draw two parallel lines cut by a transversal, measure all 8 angles, and use translations to explain why corresponding angles match.

days.title: Triangle angle sum
days.work: Tear the three corners off a paper triangle and line them up on a straight line; write an argument using parallel lines for the 180-degree sum.

days.title: Exterior angles
days.work: Explain the exterior angle theorem and solve 6 algebraic angle problems such as (2x + 10) + (3x - 5) = 120.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Unit test on rigid transformations, coordinate rules, congruence and angle relationships; reflect on two missed items.

objectives: Dilate figures from a center with a given scale factor
Describe dilations with coordinates centered at the origin

days.title: Projecting and scaling
days.work: Use a ruler to dilate a triangle from a point P with scale factor 2 and 1/2 by measuring along rays; compare side lengths and angles.

days.title: Circular grid
days.work: Dilate shapes on a circular (polar) grid, then explain why dilations preserve angles but not lengths.

days.title: Dilations on a square grid
days.work: Dilate polygons on a coordinate grid with center at the origin and write the rule (x, y) -> (kx, ky) for k = 3, 1/2 and 1.5.

days.title: Scale factor reasoning
days.work: Find the scale factor and center given a figure and image; solve 6 problems including scale factors less than 1.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: perform two dilations and find a missing scale factor and center.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on dilations by hand and with coordinates.

objectives: Define similarity as a sequence of rigid motions and dilations
Use the Angle-Angle criterion to show triangles are similar

days.title: Similarity sequences
days.work: Describe a sequence of a dilation plus rigid motions that maps one polygon to a similar one; do 4 grid problems.

days.title: Similar polygons
days.work: Test pairs of rectangles and triangles for similarity by comparing side ratios and angles; explain why all squares are similar but not all rectangles.

days.title: AA similarity
days.work: Draw two triangles with the same two angle measures but different sizes; measure sides to confirm proportional lengths and state the AA criterion.

days.title: Mirror method investigation
days.work: Use a small mirror on the floor and similar triangles to estimate the height of a tree or doorway; show the proportion and compare to a tape-measure value.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve 6 missing-side problems using similar triangles and write one AA justification.

weeks.assessment: Mirror-height lab write-up plus similarity problem set.

objectives: Use similar slope triangles to explain why slope is constant on a line
Calculate slope from a graph

days.title: Slope triangles
days.work: Draw three different slope triangles on the same line and show they are similar, so rise/run is equal for each.

days.title: Finding slope
days.work: Calculate the slope of 10 lines on grids using any two points; check with Desmos.

days.title: Writing equations from slope
days.work: Use a point (x, y) on a line through (0, 0) or (0, b) and similar triangles to derive y = mx and y = mx + b.

days.title: Unit 2 review
days.work: Mixed review of dilations, similarity and slope with a partner-check answer key.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Unit test on dilations, similarity, AA criterion and slope.

objectives: Graph proportional relationships and interpret unit rate as slope
Compare two proportional relationships shown in different ways

days.title: Rates review
days.work: Find unit rates in tables, graphs and stories (e.g., 3 miles in 45 minutes) and write y = kx equations.

days.title: Graphing proportional relationships
days.work: Graph 4 relationships, choosing scales for the axes, and identify the unit rate as the slope on each graph.

days.title: Walking-rate lab
days.work: Time yourself and a family member walking 10, 20 and 30 meters; graph both on the same axes and compare speeds using slopes.

days.title: Comparing representations
days.work: Compare a table for one cell plan and an equation for another to decide which costs more per gigabyte; justify in writing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: 5 problems comparing proportional relationships across tables, graphs and equations.

objectives: Recognize nonproportional linear relationships
Interpret slope and vertical intercept in context

days.title: Stacking cups
days.work: Measure the height of a stack of 1 to 8 paper cups, graph the data, and find the slope (height per cup) and intercept (base height).

days.title: Slope and intercept in context
days.work: For 6 stories (a gym membership with a sign-up fee, a filling pool), identify the rate of change and initial value and write y = mx + b.

days.title: More linear relationships
days.work: Match 8 equations to graphs and tables; explain what the slope and intercept mean in each context.

days.title: Translating to y = mx + b
days.work: Show that the graph of y = mx + b is a translation of y = mx by b units; graph 4 pairs in Desmos.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Water-displacement mini lab: drop marbles in a cup of water, record water level, write the linear equation; quiz on slope/intercept meaning.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on interpreting slope and intercept; lab equation.

weeks.topic: Slope signs, special lines, writing equations
objectives: Interpret negative, zero and undefined slopes
Write equations of lines from two points or a graph

days.title: Negative slope
days.work: Model a draining tank or spending a gift card balance; graph and interpret the negative rate of change.

days.title: Horizontal and vertical lines
days.work: Graph y = 4 and x = -2, find their slopes, and explain why x = -2 is not a function of x.

days.title: Slope from two points
days.work: Use the formula (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) on 10 point pairs, then write the full equation of each line.

days.title: Equations from graphs and tables
days.work: Write equations for 8 lines given as graphs or tables and check with Desmos.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: find slopes and write equations from two points, a table, a graph and a story.

weeks.topic: Solutions to linear equations in two variables
objectives: Understand that points on a line are solutions to its equation
Use linear equations such as 2x + 3y = 12 to model situations

days.title: Points on a line
days.work: Test whether 8 ordered pairs are solutions of a given equation and explain the connection to points on its graph.

days.title: Coordinates and constraints
days.work: Model a budget like $2 apples and $3 pears with $12 by writing 2x + 3y = 12; graph using intercepts.

days.title: Rearranging equations
days.work: Rewrite 6 equations into slope-intercept form and interpret the slope in context.

days.title: Unit 3 review
days.work: Complete a review stations set: proportional vs nonproportional, slope, intercepts, equations from stories.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Unit test on linear relationships.

objectives: Solve equations using balanced moves
Use the distributive property and combine like terms to solve equations

days.title: Hanger diagrams
days.work: Use hanger diagrams to reason about equations like 3x + 1 = x + 7 and record each balanced move.

days.title: Balanced moves
days.work: Decide which moves keep equations equivalent; solve 8 two-step and multi-step equations with integers.

days.title: Distributive property equations
days.work: Solve equations like 4(x - 3) = 2x + 6 and -2(5 - x) = 3x + 1, showing every step.

days.title: Error analysis
days.work: Find and correct mistakes in 5 worked solutions; write a rule for each error type (sign errors, distributing only to the first term).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: solve 8 multi-step equations and check each solution by substitution.

weeks.topic: Equations with variables on both sides and rational coefficients
objectives: Solve equations with variables on both sides including fractions and decimals
Write and solve equations from contexts

days.title: Variables on both sides
days.work: Solve 10 equations such as 7x - 4 = 3x + 12 and explain the strategy of collecting variable terms.

days.title: Fractions in equations
days.work: Clear denominators by multiplying by the LCD to solve 6 equations such as (2/3)x + 5 = (1/2)x + 7.

days.title: Decimals in equations
days.work: Solve decimal equations like 0.4(x + 5) = 1.2x - 3 and check with a calculator.

days.title: Writing equations from stories
days.work: Write and solve equations for 5 situations, e.g., two phone plans that cost the same at some number of minutes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: 6 equations with rational coefficients and 2 word problems.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on equations with rational coefficients.

objectives: Classify equations as having one, no, or infinitely many solutions
Create examples of each type

days.title: Sorting equations
days.work: Solve and sort 12 equations into one solution, no solution and infinitely many solutions; describe what the final line looks like for each.

days.title: Graphical meaning
days.work: Graph each side of an equation as a line in Desmos to see one intersection, parallel lines or the same line.

days.title: Create your own
days.work: Write two equations of each type and trade them with a family member to solve.

days.title: Context problems
days.work: Solve problems such as 'When will two savings accounts have equal balances?' and interpret no-solution answers in context.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: classify and solve 8 equations and justify one of each type in writing.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on the number of solutions.

weeks.topic: Systems of linear equations by graphing
objectives: Interpret the intersection of two lines as the solution of a system
Estimate solutions by graphing

days.title: On or off the line?
days.work: Use 'two runners' or 'two water tanks' scenarios to find when two linear quantities are equal using tables and graphs.

days.title: Graphing systems
days.work: Graph 6 systems by hand and identify the intersection point; verify it in both equations.

days.title: Special systems
days.work: Graph systems with parallel lines and identical lines and connect them to no solution and infinitely many solutions.

days.title: Writing systems from stories
days.work: Write systems for 4 contexts (e.g., ticket sales of adults and students) and estimate solutions from Desmos graphs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: solve 4 systems by graphing and interpret each solution in context.

objectives: Solve systems by substitution
Solve systems by inspection when lines are parallel or identical

days.title: Substitution with y =
days.work: Solve systems where one equation is solved for y (y = 2x + 1 and y = -x + 7) by setting expressions equal.

days.title: Substitution in general
days.work: Solve 6 systems by substitution where you must rearrange one equation first; check with Desmos.

days.title: Inspection
days.work: Decide without solving whether 6 systems have zero, one or infinitely many solutions by comparing slopes and intercepts.

days.title: Real-world systems
days.work: Solve 4 word problems, such as a coin jar with 20 coins worth $3.20 in dimes and quarters.

days.title: Unit 4 test
days.work: Unit test on linear equations and systems.

objectives: Define a function as a rule with exactly one output for each input
Identify functions from tables, graphs, mappings and descriptions

days.title: Input-output machines
days.work: Play 'guess my rule' with a family member using input/output cards, then decide which rules are functions.

days.title: Is it a function?
days.work: Classify 10 relations (tables, mapping diagrams, graphs, statements like 'a person's age -> height') as functions or not, using the vertical line test.

days.title: Function notation & language
days.work: Write statements like 'distance is a function of time' and evaluate functions from equations and graphs.

days.title: Equations for functions
days.work: Write equations for functions such as the perimeter of a square or the cost of n tickets, naming the independent and dependent variables.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: identify functions and evaluate them from 4 representations.

weeks.topic: Representing and comparing functions; semester review
objectives: Compare two functions represented in different ways
Distinguish linear from nonlinear functions

days.title: Comparing functions
days.work: Compare a function given by a table with one given by an equation (e.g., two car rental companies) and decide which grows faster.

days.title: Linear vs nonlinear
days.work: Graph y = 2x + 1, y = x^2 and A = pi r^2 from tables and explain why only the first is linear.

days.title: Semester review A
days.work: Mixed review of transformations, similarity and slope (Units 1–3) with worked corrections.

days.title: Semester review B
days.work: Mixed review of equations and systems (Unit 4) and functions; make a one-page formula and strategy sheet.

days.title: Semester 1 exam
days.work: Cumulative semester exam covering Units 1–5 so far.

weeks.topic: Linear functions, rates of change, and graphs of situations
objectives: Model situations with linear functions and interpret rate of change
Describe and sketch qualitative and piecewise graphs

days.title: Linear function models
days.work: Build functions for situations such as a phone battery draining 8% per hour from 100%; interpret rate and initial value.

days.title: Qualitative graphs
days.work: Match 6 stories (a bike ride with a stop, a filling bathtub) to graphs and describe where they increase, decrease or stay constant.

days.title: Sketching graphs
days.work: Sketch graphs from verbal descriptions and write a story for 3 given graphs.

days.title: Piecewise linear functions
days.work: Analyze a graph of a water tank filled and drained in stages; find the rate of change for each piece.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on modeling with linear functions and interpreting qualitative graphs.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on function models and graph interpretation.

objectives: Find volumes of cylinders
Use the relationship between cones and cylinders to find cone volumes

days.title: Volume of prisms review
days.work: Review V = Bh with rectangular prisms; measure a cereal box and compute its volume.

days.title: Cylinder volume
days.work: Measure 3 cans, compute V = pi r^2 h, and check by filling with water and measuring in a measuring cup (1 mL = 1 cubic cm).

days.title: Cone vs cylinder lab
days.work: Build a paper cone with the same base and height as a can; count how many cones of rice fill the can to discover V = (1/3) pi r^2 h.

days.title: Missing dimensions
days.work: Solve 6 problems finding the radius or height of cylinders and cones given volume.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: 6 cylinder and cone volume problems including a real-world one (a cone-shaped paper cup).

objectives: Find the volume of spheres and hemispheres
Analyze how volume changes as a function of radius or height

days.title: Sphere volume
days.work: Compare a sphere to a cylinder of the same radius and height 2r to justify V = (4/3) pi r^3; find volumes of 4 balls.

days.title: Composite volumes
days.work: Find volumes of composite solids like an ice-cream cone with a hemisphere on top and a grain silo.

days.title: Volume as a function
days.work: Graph volume of a cylinder as a function of height (linear) and of radius (nonlinear) in Desmos; compare.

days.title: Unit 5 review
days.work: Review functions and volume with a 12-problem mixed set.

days.title: Unit 5 test
days.work: Unit test on functions and volume.

objectives: Construct scatter plots from bivariate data
Describe association, clusters and outliers
materials: data from family members or an online data set

days.title: Collecting bivariate data
days.work: Measure arm span and height of at least 8 people (or use a provided data set) and organize in a table.

days.title: Making scatter plots
days.work: Plot arm span vs height by hand with appropriate scales; describe the pattern.

days.title: Describing association
days.work: Classify 8 scatter plots as positive, negative, or no association and linear or nonlinear; identify outliers and clusters.

days.title: Interpreting outliers
days.work: Explain possible reasons for outliers in a car age vs value data set.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: build and describe a scatter plot from a 12-row data table.

weeks.topic: Lines of fit and linear models
objectives: Informally fit a line to data and judge its fit
Use the equation of a model to make predictions and interpret slope and intercept

days.title: Fitting a line
days.work: Lay a strand of spaghetti over the arm span scatter plot to fit a line; compare lines and discuss closeness of fit.

days.title: Equations of fitted lines
days.work: Write the equation of the fitted line using two points on it; interpret the slope (cm of height per cm of arm span).

days.title: Predictions
days.work: Use models to predict values (e.g., price of a used car at 80,000 miles) and judge whether the prediction is reasonable.

days.title: Residuals
days.work: Calculate how far 5 data points are from the line and decide which of two lines fits better; check with Desmos regression.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: fit a line, write its equation and interpret slope and intercept in context.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on lines of fit and interpretation.

objectives: Construct two-way tables
Use relative frequencies to look for association in categorical data

days.title: Two-way tables
days.work: Survey 20 people (or use given data) on two yes/no questions such as 'plays an instrument' and 'likes math'; organize in a two-way table.

days.title: Relative frequency
days.work: Compute row and column relative frequencies as percents and decide whether an association exists.

days.title: Analyzing associations
days.work: Analyze 3 data sets (e.g., curfew vs chores) and write a claim with evidence from relative frequencies.

days.title: Unit 6 review
days.work: Review scatter plots, lines of fit and two-way tables with a mixed practice set.

days.title: Unit 6 test
days.work: Unit test on bivariate data.

weeks.topic: Exponent rules for products, quotients and powers
objectives: Generate exponent rules by expanding repeated multiplication
Apply product, quotient and power-of-a-power rules

days.title: Paper folding
days.work: Fold a sheet of paper in half repeatedly, record layers as powers of 2, and predict layers after 10 folds.

days.title: Multiplying powers
days.work: Expand expressions like 10^3 x 10^4 to discover a^m x a^n = a^(m+n); practice 12 problems.

days.title: Powers of powers
days.work: Expand (5^2)^3 to discover (a^m)^n = a^(mn); mix with products.

days.title: Dividing powers
days.work: Expand 7^6 / 7^2 to discover a^m / a^n = a^(m-n); solve 12 mixed problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: simplify 12 expressions using exponent rules and explain one rule with expanded form.

weeks.topic: Zero, negative exponents and different bases
objectives: Explain why a^0 = 1 and a^(-n) = 1/a^n
Simplify expressions with negative exponents and products of different bases

days.title: Zero exponents
days.work: Use a pattern table (10^3, 10^2, 10^1, ...) to justify 10^0 = 1; extend to other bases.

days.title: Negative exponents
days.work: Continue the pattern to 10^(-1), 10^(-2); rewrite 10 expressions with positive exponents.

days.title: Different bases
days.work: Use (ab)^n = a^n b^n to simplify expressions like 2^3 x 5^3 = 10^3; evaluate 8 expressions.

days.title: Mixed practice
days.work: Complete a 20-problem mixed exponent card sort, matching equivalent expressions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: evaluate and simplify 12 expressions with zero and negative exponents.

objectives: Write large and small numbers in scientific notation
Compare quantities using powers of 10

days.title: Powers of 10 on a number line
days.work: Place numbers like 3 x 10^5 and 7 x 10^(-3) on number lines labeled with powers of 10.

days.title: Writing scientific notation
days.work: Convert 12 quantities (distance to the Sun, mass of a dust grain, U.S. population) to and from scientific notation.

days.title: Comparing magnitudes
days.work: Use powers of 10 to estimate how many times larger one quantity is (Earth vs Moon mass, a blue whale vs an ant).

days.title: Using a calculator
days.work: Read calculator 'E' notation and convert planetary data from NASA into scientific notation.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: convert, compare and order 10 numbers in scientific notation.

objectives: Multiply and divide numbers in scientific notation
Add and subtract numbers in scientific notation and choose sensible units

days.title: Multiplying & dividing
days.work: Compute products and quotients like (3 x 10^8)(2 x 10^3) and adjust answers to proper scientific notation.

days.title: Adding & subtracting
days.work: Rewrite with a common power of 10 before adding/subtracting; complete 8 problems.

days.title: Space math
days.work: Calculate how long light takes to travel from the Sun to each planet using distance / (3 x 10^8 m/s).

days.title: Unit 7 review
days.work: Review exponent rules and scientific notation with a self-checking puzzle.

days.title: Unit 7 test
days.work: Unit test on exponents and scientific notation.

weeks.topic: Square roots and side lengths of squares
objectives: Find areas of tilted squares on a grid and relate side length to square root
Estimate square roots between consecutive integers

days.title: Tilted squares
days.work: Draw squares on a grid with tilted sides; find their areas by decomposing or surrounding with a larger square.

days.title: Side lengths as square roots
days.work: Write side lengths of those squares as square roots (e.g., sqrt 10) and estimate each between two whole numbers.

days.title: Perfect squares
days.work: Memorize perfect squares 1–225; solve x^2 = p for 10 values of p including non-perfect squares.

days.title: Estimating roots
days.work: Estimate sqrt 50, sqrt 72 and sqrt 130 to the tenth by guess-and-check squaring; check with a calculator.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: tilted-square areas, solving x^2 = p and placing square roots on a number line.

weeks.topic: The Pythagorean theorem and its converse
objectives: Explain a visual proof of the Pythagorean theorem
Use the converse to determine whether a triangle is a right triangle

days.title: Finding a pattern
days.work: Draw right triangles on a grid, build squares on each side and record areas to discover a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

days.title: Visual proof
days.work: Cut and rearrange four congruent right triangles inside a square (the 'two squares' proof) and explain in writing why it proves the theorem.

days.title: Finding unknown sides
days.work: Solve 10 problems finding a missing leg or hypotenuse, leaving irrational answers as square roots and as decimals.

days.title: The converse
days.work: Test side lengths (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 6-7-9) with the converse; use a 3-4-5 knotted string to check a corner of a room for square.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: explain the proof in your own words and solve 6 problems including converse questions.

objectives: Apply the theorem in 2-D and 3-D real-world problems
Find distance between two points on the coordinate plane

days.title: Real-world right triangles
days.work: Solve problems with ladders, TV screen diagonals and ramps; measure a TV to check its advertised diagonal.

days.title: 3-D diagonals
days.work: Find the longest straight object that fits in a shoe box by computing the space diagonal; verify with a measured straw or string.

days.title: Distance on the coordinate plane
days.work: Draw the right triangle under segments between points and find 8 distances.

days.title: Mixed applications
days.work: Solve 6 multi-step problems such as walking diagonally across a park vs around it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: 3 real-world, 2 three-dimensional and 3 coordinate distance problems.

weeks.topic: Cube roots and rational vs irrational numbers
objectives: Solve x^3 = p using cube roots
Convert repeating decimals to fractions and classify numbers as rational or irrational

days.title: Cube roots
days.work: Build cubes of side 1–5 with sugar or snap cubes; solve x^3 = p for perfect and non-perfect cubes and estimate.

days.title: Decimal expansions
days.work: Use long division to write fractions such as 5/11 and 7/12 as decimals; identify repeating patterns.

days.title: Repeating decimals to fractions
days.work: Use the 'multiply by 10^n and subtract' method to convert 0.7777..., 0.272727... and 1.16666... to fractions.

days.title: Rational or irrational?
days.work: Sort 16 numbers (sqrt 16, pi, 0.121212..., sqrt 2, 22/7) and justify each placement.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: cube roots, conversions and classification of real numbers.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on cube roots and the real number system.

objectives: Approximate irrational numbers to the hundredth
Compare and order irrational and rational numbers on a number line

days.title: Zooming in on sqrt 2
days.work: Use successive number lines to trap sqrt 2 between tenths, then hundredths, without a calculator.

days.title: Ordering real numbers
days.work: Order sets like {pi, sqrt 10, 3.1, 22/7, 3.15} on a number line with justification.

days.title: Estimating expressions
days.work: Estimate values like pi^2 and 2 sqrt 5 + 1 and compare estimates to calculator values.

days.title: Unit 8 review
days.work: Mixed review: roots, Pythagorean theorem, distance and real numbers.

days.title: Unit 8 test
days.work: Unit test on the Pythagorean theorem and irrational numbers.

objectives: Break large estimation problems into smaller computable parts
Use scientific notation and volume to estimate quantities

days.title: What is a Fermi problem?
days.work: Estimate how many ping-pong balls fit in your house's living room using volume of spheres and a room measurement; list assumptions.

days.title: Fermi problem 2
days.work: Estimate how many heartbeats you will have in your lifetime and express in scientific notation.

days.title: Choose your own
days.work: Pick a question (e.g., how many pizzas are eaten in California per year), research a few facts and build an estimate.

days.title: Presentation
days.work: Present your Fermi estimate on a poster with the steps, assumptions and an order-of-magnitude reasonableness check.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Self- and parent-assess the poster with a rubric; complete 6 cumulative review problems on exponents and volume.

weeks.topic: Modeling project: planning a small business
objectives: Use linear functions to model cost and revenue
Use a system to find a break-even point

days.title: Business idea and costs
days.work: Choose a small business (lemonade stand, dog walking, baking) and write a cost function with fixed and per-item costs.

days.title: Revenue and break-even
days.work: Write a revenue function and solve the system to find the break-even point; graph both in Desmos.

days.title: Using data
days.work: Use a short table of sales vs price (given or surveyed) to fit a line and predict sales at a new price.

days.title: Final review
days.work: Cumulative review of all units using a 30-problem mixed set; mark items to revisit.

days.title: Project presentation
days.work: Present the business plan with graphs, break-even point and recommendations.

objectives: Demonstrate mastery of Grade 8 standards
Reflect on growth over the year

days.title: Review: geometry
days.work: Review transformations, similarity, angles, Pythagorean theorem and volume with 15 problems.

days.title: Review: algebra
days.work: Review linear equations, systems, functions, exponents and scientific notation with 15 problems.

days.title: Final exam part 1
days.work: Take part 1 of the cumulative final (geometry, number system, data).

days.title: Final exam part 2
days.work: Take part 2 of the cumulative final (expressions, equations, functions).

days.title: Reflection & portfolio
days.work: Correct final exam errors and write a one-page reflection on your three most improved skills; organize the math portfolio for Algebra I.

weeks.assessment: Cumulative final exam and portfolio reflection.
